title: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP) Golden and Green Visas
source: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)
publisher: Government of the United Arab Emirates
content:
The United Arab Emirates provides long-term self-sponsored residency under the Golden Visa (10-year residency) and Green Visa (5-year residency) tracks administered by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP).

The 10-year Golden Visa is granted to investors, real estate owners (purchasing property valued at AED 2,000,000 or more), entrepreneurs, exceptional talents, scientists, and outstanding specialists earning a minimum monthly salary of AED 30,000. Golden Visa holders are exempt from the standard rule requiring return to the UAE every six months to maintain visa validity.

All residents in the UAE must obtain a biometric Emirates ID card issued by the ICP, which is legally mandatory for banking, rental contracts, mobile lines, and domestic regulatory transactions.

title: General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA) Dubai Residency Permits
source: General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA Dubai)
content:
The General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA Dubai) manages residency issuance, entry permits, and immigration control across the Emirate of Dubai.

Foreign employees are sponsored by Dubai mainland companies or free zone entities (such as DIFC, DMCC, or DAFZA). The residency process encompasses an entry permit, mandatory medical fitness screening (blood test for communicable diseases and chest X-ray at authorized DHA centres), Emirates ID biometric capture, and electronic residence visa issuance.

Residency visas are generally issued for two or three years depending on employer jurisdiction and can be renewed indefinitely so long as employment remains active and valid.

title: Roads and Transport Authority (RTA Dubai) Public Transport and Nol Contactless Card System
content:
The Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) operates public transport across Dubai, including the driverless Dubai Metro (Red and Green Lines), Dubai Tram, Dubai Water Taxis, and comprehensive public bus fleets.

Public transit in Dubai is fully cashless using the electronic Nol Card (Silver, Gold, Personal, and Red ticket variants). The transit network is divided into 7 geographic fare zones, with fares tiered by whether the trip covers 1 zone, 2 adjacent zones, or more than 2 zones.

The Red Line connects Dubai International Airport (Terminals 1 and 3) directly with major residential and commercial hubs including Deira, Downtown Dubai (Burj Khalifa / Dubai Mall), Dubai Marina, and Jebel Ali / Expo City.

title: Dubai Health Authority (DHA) Mandatory Health Insurance Scheme (ISAHD)
content:
Under Dubai Health Insurance Law No. 11 of 2013 (the Insurance System for Advancing Healthcare in Dubai - ISAHD), health insurance is mandatory for all citizens and residents in the Emirate of Dubai.

Employers are legally obligated to provide and pay for health insurance coverage for all employees from the date of employment without deducting premiums from employee salaries. For lower-income workers earning under AED 4,000 monthly, employers must provide the Essential Benefits Plan (EBP).

Sponsors of dependents (spouses, children, domestic workers) are personally responsible for purchasing health insurance policies for their sponsored family members. Proof of valid health insurance is an electronic prerequisite for the issuance or renewal of any Dubai residence visa.

title: Dubai Land Department (DLD) Ejari Tenancy Contracts and RERA Rental Valuation Index
source: Dubai Land Department (DLD) / Real Estate Regulatory Agency (RERA)
content:
All residential lease contracts in the Emirate of Dubai must be registered with the Dubai Land Department (DLD) on the Ejari system (Arabic for 'my rent'). An Ejari certificate is the only legally binding proof of tenancy and is required to connect DEWA electricity and water utilities, sponsor family residence visas, and access telecom home internet.

Residential leases typically run for one year paid via bank cheques (single cheque or quarterly installments). The standard security deposit is 5% of annual rent for unfurnished properties and 10% for furnished properties.

Rent increases upon contract renewal are strictly governed by the RERA Rental Calculator (Decree No. 43 of 2013), capping potential increases (0% to 20%) based on how much the existing rent sits below the official average market rent for that specific area.
